stem:
Soham heats a solid wax crayon. At its melting point the wax turns soft and liquid.

Which claim correctly explains melting and why the melting point identifies that change?

options.text: Heating makes the particles vibrate more until they leave fixed positions; the melting point is the temperature at which this change begins.
Heating pushes the particles closer until they stop vibrating; the melting point is when vibration stops.
Heating turns the solid straight into gas; the melting point is the boiling temperature.
Melting begins at any temperature once the crayon is stirred.

teacher.key_rationale: Heat increases particle vibration until particles leave fixed positions and the solid becomes liquid. The melting point is that temperature at atmospheric pressure, so it identifies the change. Melting is not boiling, and stirring does not replace the temperature condition.
